answer: Anchoring AI verification in a static harbor like a sheltered lagoon risks spoofing, so dynamic networks must enforce a continuous proof-of-work burn tied to physical compute cycles. Every transaction requires validating a cryptographic signal against rapidly changing nonce targets, imposing a severe hardware and power cost on any botnet trying to spawn duplicate identities. If a stray sparrow consumes more resources than its designated fuel allocation, the automated circuit breaker isolates the rogue node immediately.
